traps.trap: FNAC is the first investigation for a solitary thyroid nodule (merges TR2: radionuclide scan first)

probes.stem_idea: Euthyroid adult with a solitary painless nodule. Which is the FIRST investigation by current practice?
probes.correct: Serum TSH with neck ultrasound
probes.note: FNAC is the old PYQ key for 'first'; the scan is the TR2 sub-trap (function test placed too early). Thyroglobulin is partial (K69), kept as a plausible marker option.

probes.stem_idea: Order the work-up: TSH, ultrasound, scan if TSH low, FNAC by ultrasound pattern and size. Which comes first, and which test answers 'what is the nature of the nodule'?
probes.correct: TSH and ultrasound first; FNAC answers the nature of the nodule
distractor_set: FNAC first, then ultrasound to confirm
Scan first to split hot from cold, then FNAC
FNAC and scan together as the first step
probes.note: Second probe adds the 'investigation of choice' phrase so the learner must separate 'first' from 'of choice'. Add a short contrast probe: hot nodule with low TSH needs scan, not FNAC (K55, K56).

traps.diagnoses: Learner treats 'investigation of choice' and 'first investigation' as one question and carries the old key forward.
traps.first_wrong_step: Reads 'investigation of choice for the nature of a nodule' as 'the first test to order', skipping TSH and ultrasound that decide who needs FNAC.

repair.strategy: E5: teach both - PYQs expected FNAC first; current practice is TSH and ultrasound first, FNAC is the investigation of choice for nature

traps.retest: sequence-form probe in the work-up segment, then a mixed stem in the exam-traps segment with a hot-nodule twist
traps.report_hint: Avoided: separates 'first' from 'of choice'. Fell and recovered: now answers both the old key and the current one. Stayed fallen: still answers FNAC to 'first'; tell them to read whether the stem asks first or nature.

traps.trap: Follicular carcinoma is the most common thyroid cancer

probes.stem_idea: Most common thyroid cancer overall, then the same question in a hill-region iodine-deficient population (relative proportion).
probes.correct: Papillary overall; follicular is relatively more frequent only in iodine deficiency
distractor_set: Papillary in every population including iodine-deficient areas
probes.note: The qualifier (iodine-deficient, relative) is the discriminating feature; option 2 is correct-adjacent (papillary is still the overall answer) so it is partial.

probes.stem_idea: Two regions side by side (iodine-sufficient vs iodine-deficient): which cancer gains share where?
probes.correct: Papillary in the iodine-sufficient region, relatively more follicular in the deficient one
distractor_set: Papillary falls to a minority in both

traps.diagnoses: Learner stops reading at 'most common' and ignores or inverts the geographic qualifier.
traps.first_wrong_step: Sees an iodine-deficiency clue and answers follicular for 'most common' without checking whether the stem asks overall or relative frequency.

repair.strategy: E7: highlight the qualifier; contrast the two settings

traps.retest: contrast probe later; also appears as a mixed 'most common' round in exam traps
traps.report_hint: Avoided: reads the geographic qualifier. Recovered: now flips answer only when the setting says so. Fallen: defaults to one answer whatever the setting.

traps.trap: Cytology or frozen section can diagnose follicular carcinoma

probes.stem_idea: FNAC reports a follicular neoplasm (Bethesda IV). What finding on which test is needed to call it carcinoma?
probes.correct: Capsular or vascular invasion on histology of the resected lobe
distractor_set: Nuclear grooves and ground-glass nuclei on FNAC
Repeat FNAC with an ultrasound-guided needle
probes.note: Distractor 1 carries the papillary test to a follicular lesion (also a TR5 look-alike signal); keep it mapped to TR5 so it diagnoses one error.

probes.stem_idea: Which statement about follicular carcinoma is NOT true?
probes.correct: Cytology can reliably separate adenoma from carcinoma
distractor_set: It is diagnosed on histology by capsular or vascular invasion
Bethesda IV is the usual FNAC report
Frozen section is of limited value
probes.note: Distractors here are true statements; the trap is believing they are false. A learner holding TR4 will reject the correct key.

probes.stem_idea: Surgeon asks for frozen section during lobectomy for Bethesda IV; what does the learner expect to learn?
probes.correct: Frozen section cannot reliably show invasion, so final histology decides
distractor_set: Frozen section confirms carcinoma so total thyroidectomy is done at once
Frozen section rules out carcinoma, so no more tissue is needed
Frozen section decides adenoma versus carcinoma by nuclear features

traps.diagnoses: Learner believes a cytology-type test can make the follicular diagnosis, as it does for papillary.
traps.first_wrong_step: Carries the 'nuclear features on FNAC' logic from papillary to follicular lesions, forgetting that the follicular diagnosis needs invasion, which only histology across the capsule shows.

repair.strategy: E8: ladder of tests - what FNAC answers (nuclear features, so papillary) versus what histology answers (invasion, so follicular)

traps.retest: which-is-not and frozen-section vignette in later segments
traps.report_hint: Avoided: knows FNAC reports IV and histology decides. Recovered: separates what each test sees. Fallen: expects cytology to name follicular cancer; stress 'invasion is a histology feature'.

traps.trap: Papillary carcinoma is diagnosed by its papillary architecture (merges TR9: psammoma bodies are PTC-exclusive)

probes.stem_idea: Which feature is the DIAGNOSTIC criterion for papillary carcinoma?
probes.correct: Optically clear nuclei with grooves and pseudoinclusions
probes.note: Psammoma bodies are supportive, not diagnostic and not exclusive (TR9 sub-trap).

probes.stem_idea: Follicular-pattern tumour with no papillae but ground-glass nuclei: papillary or follicular?
probes.correct: Papillary carcinoma (follicular variant), because of the nuclei
distractor_set: Follicular carcinoma, because there are no papillae
Follicular adenoma, because it is encapsulated
Anaplastic carcinoma, because the pattern is atypical

probes.stem_idea: Which tumour is NOT associated with psammoma bodies? Listed with PTC, serous ovarian tumour, meningioma, mesothelioma, and follicular carcinoma.
probes.correct: Follicular carcinoma
probes.note: A learner who thinks psammoma bodies are thyroid-only will choose an off-thyroid tumour as the 'not' answer.

traps.diagnoses: Learner defines papillary carcinoma by the name's architecture and by one pairing, rather than by the nuclear features.
traps.first_wrong_step: Takes the name 'papillary' as the test, so a tumour without papillae is not called papillary and psammoma bodies are treated as exclusive.

repair.strategy: E1: contrasting cases - papillary (nuclei decide, papillae and psammoma are supportive) against follicular (no PTC nuclei, invasion decides)

traps.retest: contrast and which-is-not probes in later segments
traps.report_hint: Avoided: diagnoses on nuclei. Recovered: now names the follicular variant as papillary. Fallen: still tied to papillae; revisit 'nuclei decide'.

traps.trap: An encapsulated follicular variant of PTC is a carcinoma

probes.stem_idea: Which of these is classified as a NON-malignant neoplasm since 2016?
probes.correct: NIFTP (non-invasive follicular neoplasm with papillary-like nuclei)
distractor_set: Follicular variant of papillary carcinoma with invasion
Tall cell variant of papillary carcinoma

probes.stem_idea: Lobectomy specimen: encapsulated, follicular pattern, papillary-like nuclei, no capsular or vascular invasion. Best classification and consequence?
probes.correct: NIFTP, not a carcinoma, so lobectomy alone is enough
distractor_set: Encapsulated follicular variant of PTC, a carcinoma needing completion thyroidectomy

traps.diagnoses: Learner uses the older key that counts any follicular variant with papillary nuclei as cancer.
traps.first_wrong_step: Sees papillary-like nuclei and stops, without asking whether invasion is present.

repair.strategy: E5: teach both - PYQs treated encapsulated follicular variant as cancer; since 2016 the non-invasive form is NIFTP

traps.retest: vignette later, plus a 'which is malignant' list in exam traps
traps.report_hint: Avoided: knows NIFTP. Recovered: separates invasive from non-invasive. Fallen: still calls any follicular variant cancer.

traps.trap: The AJCC age cut-off for DTC staging is 45 years

probes.stem_idea: AJCC 8th edition age cut-off for DTC staging (PYQ key says 45).
probes.correct: 55 years

probes.stem_idea: A 50-year-old with DTC and lung metastasis: AJCC 8th stage?
probes.correct: Stage II, because under 55 distant metastasis is stage II
distractor_set: Stage IVB, because of distant spread
Stage I, because DTC is low grade

traps.diagnoses: Learner holds the 7th edition cut-off and applies it to current staging.
traps.first_wrong_step: Recalls the number 45 as fixed and does not ask which edition the stem uses.

repair.strategy: E5: teach both - PYQs expected 45; AJCC 8th uses 55 and under 55 there are only stages I and II

traps.retest: vignette in a later segment
traps.report_hint: Avoided: states 55. Recovered: handles under-55 staging. Fallen: still uses 45; flag edition-awareness.

traps.trap: Total thyroidectomy is the treatment for all differentiated thyroid cancer (merges TR19: one size cut-off)

probes.stem_idea: 1.5 cm unifocal papillary carcinoma, intrathyroidal, no nodes, no radiation history. Acceptable surgery by current guidance?
probes.correct: Lobectomy or total thyroidectomy, both acceptable
distractor_set: Total thyroidectomy only, with central dissection
Total thyroidectomy followed by lateral neck dissection
probes.note: Neck-dissection option is a sub-trap from the dropped TR31 and kept as partial so it does not diagnose a second wrong model; mark partial in authoring if TR31 is not branched.

probes.stem_idea: Match each case to surgery: 0.8 cm node-negative microcarcinoma; 2 cm low-risk unifocal; 5 cm tumour.
probes.correct: Lobectomy or surveillance; either operation; total thyroidectomy
distractor_set: Total thyroidectomy for the first two, lobectomy for the 5 cm tumour

probes.stem_idea: Treatment of choice for DTC needing surgery: what did PYQs expect, what does ATA 2015 accept?
probes.correct: Total thyroidectomy was expected; lobectomy is accepted when low risk
distractor_set: Lobectomy was expected; total thyroidectomy is now routine
Total thyroidectomy is mandatory for every DTC today
Radioiodine alone is accepted for low-risk disease

traps.diagnoses: Learner applies the classic key to every DTC and does not use size and risk to choose the operation.
traps.first_wrong_step: Hears 'treatment of choice' as unconditional and does not check tumour size, nodes, extension and prior irradiation.

repair.strategy: E5: teach both - PYQs expected total thyroidectomy; current guidance accepts lobectomy for low-risk 1-4 cm and lobectomy or surveillance below 1 cm; show the bands as a ladder

traps.retest: numbers probe mid-module, then recognition in exam traps
traps.report_hint: Avoided: picks the operation by risk. Recovered: gives both key and current practice. Fallen: still one operation for all; revisit the size bands.

traps.trap: A lateral aberrant thyroid is ectopic thyroid tissue

probes.stem_idea: 'Lateral aberrant thyroid' in the neck is actually which entity?
probes.correct: Lymph-node metastasis from papillary carcinoma
distractor_set: Ectopic thyroid tissue in the lateral neck

probes.stem_idea: Young woman with a firm lateral neck mass; FNAC shows thyroid follicular cells with papillary nuclei. What to do next?
probes.correct: Look for a primary papillary carcinoma in the thyroid
distractor_set: Excise it as benign ectopic thyroid
Give radioiodine without imaging the thyroid

traps.diagnoses: Learner trusts the name 'aberrant thyroid' and reads a lateral neck mass as ectopia.
traps.first_wrong_step: Takes the label literally instead of recalling that thyroid tissue in a lateral node is metastatic.

repair.strategy: E10: pair recall - 'lateral aberrant thyroid' belongs with papillary nodal metastasis; contrast with midline thyroglossal tissue

traps.retest: vignette later
traps.report_hint: Avoided: pairs the name with nodal metastasis. Fallen: relies on names; teach by site.

traps.trap: Papillary spreads by blood and follicular spreads by lymphatics

probes.stem_idea: Predict, then show: a tumour that invades the capsule and vessels. Which route does follicular carcinoma take and where does it land?
probes.correct: Blood-borne to lung and bone
distractor_set: Blood to lung and neck nodes
probes.note: Option 2 mixes the right route with the nodal site, so it feeds TR12.

probes.stem_idea: Two patients: one with a lateral neck node and a small thyroid primary; one with a pathological fracture and thyroid nodule. Match the cancers.
probes.correct: Papillary with the nodal presentation; follicular with the bone presentation
distractor_set: Follicular with the nodal presentation; papillary with the bone presentation

traps.diagnoses: Learner holds the two spread routes as a reversed pair.
traps.first_wrong_step: Does not link the follicular diagnostic feature (vascular invasion) to blood spread, so the route is guessed.

repair.strategy: E3: predict-then-show - invasion of vessels predicts blood spread for follicular; papillary sits in lymphatics

traps.retest: contrast probe, then a route-of-spread item in exam traps
traps.report_hint: Avoided: routes correct. Recovered: derives route from invasion. Fallen: pairs reversed; teach vascular invasion as the cue.

traps.trap: Cervical lymph nodes are the usual site of follicular carcinoma spread (merges TR13: medullary and anaplastic counted as DTC)

probes.stem_idea: Which is NOT a common site of distant spread of follicular carcinoma?
probes.correct: Cervical lymph nodes
probes.note: A learner holding TR12 sees nodes as a true site and picks a true site as the 'not'. Brain is a rare site kept as a plausible filler, partial.

probes.stem_idea: Which is NOT a differentiated thyroid cancer?
probes.correct: Medullary carcinoma
probes.note: Sub-trap TR13: those holding 'all thyroid malignancies are DTC' reject the key. Anaplastic carcinoma can replace medullary on the retest.

probes.stem_idea: Biopsy-proven follicular carcinoma with no neck nodes. A resident says 'nodes are probably involved'. What is the best response?
probes.correct: Node metastasis is uncommon in follicular carcinoma; look for lung and bone
distractor_set: Nodes are the usual first site, so do central dissection
Nodes and lung are equally common
Nodes are spared only in medullary carcinoma

traps.diagnoses: Learner builds the site and type lists by 'thyroid cancer spreads to nodes' and 'thyroid cancer is DTC' instead of from the cell of origin and route.
traps.first_wrong_step: Adds the familiar item (nodes, or any thyroid malignancy) to the set without testing it against blood spread or follicular-cell origin.

repair.strategy: E2: rebuild the set from its logic - follicular spreads by blood to lung and bone; DTC means follicular-cell cancers (papillary, follicular, oncocytic)

traps.retest: second which-is-not in a different list, then the vignette
traps.report_hint: Avoided: sets built from logic. Recovered: now excludes nodes from the follicular set. Fallen: adds familiar items to lists; teach set-building.

traps.trap: A negative radioiodine scan rules out recurrence when thyroglobulin is raised

probes.stem_idea: After total thyroidectomy and radioiodine, Tg is rising and the whole-body radioiodine scan is negative. Next step?
probes.correct: FDG-PET to look for radioiodine-refractory disease
distractor_set: Reassure, since the scan is negative

probes.stem_idea: Why does a rising Tg with a negative iodine scan point to a particular kind of tumour behaviour?
probes.correct: Tumour still makes Tg but has lost iodine uptake
distractor_set: The scan is more sensitive than Tg, so Tg is false
No tumour remains, and Tg is from normal tissue

traps.diagnoses: Learner uses the same test again instead of switching to one that does not need iodine uptake.
traps.first_wrong_step: Trusts the scan over the marker and does not ask whether the tumour still takes up iodine.

repair.strategy: E8: ladder of follow-up tests - Tg detects, iodine scan finds iodine-avid disease, PET finds the iodine-negative disease

traps.retest: mechanism probe later; follow-up ladder in consolidation
traps.report_hint: Avoided: changes the test. Fallen: repeats the scan; teach refractory disease.

traps.trap: Radioiodine is given to every DTC patient

probes.stem_idea: Low-risk unifocal intrathyroidal papillary carcinoma after total thyroidectomy. Radioiodine?
probes.correct: Not routinely given for ATA low risk
distractor_set: Radioiodine ablation as standard for every DTC
Radioiodine only if the tumour is follicular

probes.stem_idea: Two patients after thyroidectomy: low risk, intrathyroidal; high risk with distant metastasis. Who needs radioiodine?
probes.correct: The high-risk patient with metastasis only

traps.diagnoses: Learner treats radioiodine as a routine adjuvant and drops the risk qualifier.
traps.first_wrong_step: Takes 'standard adjuvant' as universal without stratifying by ATA risk.

repair.strategy: E7: highlight the qualifier - contrast low-risk and high-risk settings

traps.retest: contrast probe later; case with a TSH-prep twist in management
traps.report_hint: Avoided: stratifies by risk. Fallen: gives radioiodine to all; revisit ATA risk.

traps.trap: Bethesda II nodule needs surgery

probes.stem_idea: Asymptomatic 2 cm nodule, FNAC Bethesda II. Next step?
probes.correct: Clinical and ultrasound follow-up

probes.stem_idea: Bethesda II with compressive symptoms versus without. When does a benign report lead to surgery?
probes.correct: Only for compressive symptoms or cosmesis
distractor_set: Always, since the nodule is large
Only after repeat FNAC shows malignancy

traps.diagnoses: Learner skips the benign follow-up step and treats any cytology report as a path to operation.
traps.first_wrong_step: Reads 'nodule with cytology' as 'send for surgery' without matching the report category to its action.

repair.strategy: E9: order the steps - report category first, action second; Bethesda II follows with surveillance

traps.retest: sequence probe, then Bethesda IV versus II in the management case
traps.report_hint: Avoided: surveillance for II. Fallen: operates on benign reports; teach category-to-action.

traps.trap: Bethesda IV and V mean the same management

probes.stem_idea: Match Bethesda IV and V to name and action.
probes.correct: IV follicular neoplasm: diagnostic lobectomy or molecular testing; V suspicious for malignancy: cancer surgery
distractor_set: IV suspicious for malignancy: cancer surgery
IV and V both follicular neoplasm: lobectomy

probes.stem_idea: FNAC: 'follicular neoplasm'. Which category and what next?
probes.correct: Bethesda IV; diagnostic lobectomy or molecular testing

traps.diagnoses: Learner swaps adjacent category numbers.
traps.first_wrong_step: Recalls the list as a run of numbers without tying each to a word and an action.

repair.strategy: E6: anchor each number to its word and action; retest in another form

traps.retest: vignette with the name given and number asked
traps.report_hint: Avoided: numbers anchored. Fallen: swaps IV and V; teach name-to-action.

traps.trap: Loss of high-pitched voice is recurrent laryngeal nerve injury

probes.stem_idea: After thyroidectomy a singer reports voice fatigue and loss of high pitch; no hoarseness or stridor. Nerve injured?
probes.correct: External branch of the superior laryngeal nerve
distractor_set: Internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve

probes.stem_idea: Pair each nerve with its symptom: hoarseness; stridor; loss of pitch.
probes.correct: Unilateral RLN with hoarseness; bilateral RLN with stridor; external branch of SLN with loss of pitch
distractor_set: RLN with loss of pitch; SLN with hoarseness; bilateral RLN with stridor
Unilateral RLN with stridor; bilateral RLN with hoarseness; SLN with loss of pitch

traps.diagnoses: Learner names the more familiar laryngeal nerve for any post-thyroidectomy voice change.
traps.first_wrong_step: Does not separate pitch change (cricothyroid, external branch of SLN) from hoarseness (RLN).

repair.strategy: E1: contrasting cases - symptom to nerve, with cricothyroid as the discriminator

traps.retest: contrast probe in the complications segment
traps.report_hint: Avoided: separates the nerves. Fallen: RLN for every voice change; teach cricothyroid.

traps.trap: The most common complication after thyroidectomy is nerve injury or bleeding

probes.stem_idea: Most common complication after total thyroidectomy?
probes.correct: Transient hypocalcaemia from hypoparathyroidism

probes.stem_idea: Day 2 after total thyroidectomy: perioral tingling and a positive Chvostek sign. Diagnosis and why it is the commonest problem?
probes.correct: Hypocalcaemia from parathyroid hypofunction

traps.diagnoses: Learner equates the most dramatic complication with the most common.
traps.first_wrong_step: Ranks complications by how memorable they are rather than by frequency.

repair.strategy: E4: show the exact qualifier - most common (transient hypocalcaemia) versus most feared (nerve injury, bleeding)

traps.retest: vignette form later
traps.report_hint: Avoided: knows commonest. Fallen: picks the dramatic complication; teach common versus feared.

traps.trap: A neck haematoma is first managed by reintubation

probes.stem_idea: Post-thyroidectomy neck swelling with stridor in the ward. First action?
probes.correct: Open the wound at the bedside to evacuate the clot
distractor_set: Intubate first in the operating theatre
Shift to the operating theatre before any step

probes.stem_idea: Two patients with stridor after thyroidectomy: one with a tense swelling, one with a flat neck and hoarse voice. Which one has the bedside-opening step?
probes.correct: The one with a tense neck swelling
distractor_set: The one with a flat neck

traps.diagnoses: Learner jumps to the airway device and skips the step that removes the cause.
traps.first_wrong_step: Treats airway as the first action in all cases without noting that a haematoma compresses the airway from outside, so releasing it comes first.

repair.strategy: E9: order the steps - release the clot, then secure the airway

traps.retest: vignette later, with a stridor-but-flat-neck twist
traps.report_hint: Avoided: opens wound first. Fallen: airway device first; teach cause-first logic.

traps.trap: TSH should be suppressed before radioiodine ablation (merges TR17: one TSH target for every risk group)

probes.stem_idea: Predict, then show: radioiodine is taken up through TSH-driven iodine uptake. What TSH state is needed before the dose?
probes.correct: High TSH, by hormone withdrawal or recombinant TSH
distractor_set: Normal TSH on a stable dose

probes.stem_idea: TSH goal before ablation versus after surgery for follow-up, with the risk-matched target (below 0.1 for high risk; low-normal for low risk).
probes.correct: High before ablation; suppressed after, with deeper suppression in high-risk disease
distractor_set: Below 0.1 for every patient after surgery

traps.diagnoses: Learner applies the follow-up logic ('suppress TSH') to the ablation phase, reversing the mechanism, and holds one target for every risk group.
traps.first_wrong_step: Does not separate the phase that needs TSH to drive iodine uptake from the phase that needs TSH low to starve residual tumour.

repair.strategy: E3: predict-then-show - uptake needs TSH, so raise it before the dose, then suppress it afterwards

traps.retest: contrast probe later; mixed in a management case
traps.report_hint: Avoided: phases separated. Fallen: suppresses before radioiodine; teach TSH drives uptake.

traps.trap: A low thyroglobulin is reassuring when anti-thyroglobulin antibodies are present

probes.stem_idea: Post-thyroidectomy follow-up: Tg undetectable but anti-Tg antibodies are high. Interpretation?
probes.correct: Tg is unreliable; the antibodies spoil the assay, so image and trend

probes.stem_idea: Which test must be measured together with thyroglobulin?
probes.correct: Anti-thyroglobulin antibodies

traps.diagnoses: Learner reads the tumour marker alone, without the assay-interference qualifier.
traps.first_wrong_step: Accepts a low Tg value without asking whether the assay can be trusted.

repair.strategy: E7: highlight the qualifier - antibodies make Tg unreliable

traps.retest: recognition probe later, then a follow-up case
traps.report_hint: Avoided: checks antibodies. Fallen: reads Tg alone; teach the qualifier.

traps.trap: Calcitonin is the marker for differentiated thyroid cancer

probes.stem_idea: Tumour marker for follow-up of papillary and follicular carcinoma?
probes.correct: Serum thyroglobulin

probes.stem_idea: Match marker to tumour: thyroglobulin, calcitonin; papillary/follicular, medullary.
probes.correct: Thyroglobulin with DTC; calcitonin with medullary carcinoma
distractor_set: Calcitonin with DTC; thyroglobulin with medullary

traps.diagnoses: Learner links the wrong thyroid marker to DTC.
traps.first_wrong_step: Treats all thyroid tumour markers as interchangeable and does not tie each to its cell of origin.

repair.strategy: E10: pair recall - follicular cell makes thyroglobulin; parafollicular C cell makes calcitonin

traps.retest: contrast probe later; consolidation card
traps.report_hint: Avoided: pairs markers by cell. Fallen: swaps markers; teach by cell of origin.

dropped.reason: merged into TR1 as a distractor and sub-trap (scan first)
merged into TR5 (psammoma bodies as an exclusive pairing)
merged into TR12 as a second list probe (DTC membership)
merged into TR27 (TSH target by risk)
merged into TR8 (size bands for surgery)
cap of 20; medium yield, E4 superlative covered by TR25
cap of 20; medium yield, sequencing error covered by TR21 and TR26
cap of 20; medium yield, number swap covered by TR22 and TR7
cap of 20; medium yield, list error covered by TR12
cap of 20; low yield, thyroglobulin used pre-operatively appears only as a distractor in TR1
cap of 20; medium yield, appears only as a partial distractor in TR8
cap of 20; medium yield, TKI qualifier overlaps TR16 and TR20

probe_plan: Backbone traps: TR1 (first test versus test of choice) opens the work-up and anchors TR4 (what FNAC can and cannot diagnose), which leans on TR5 (papillary diagnosed by nuclei, follicular by invasion), so meet TR5 and TR4 together early as one contrast, then re-test TR4 in a which-is-not and a frozen-section vignette. TR11 and TR12 form the spread block (reversed route, then the list of sites and DTC membership) and TR10 follows as a look-alike of nodal spread. TR3 and TR6 are small qualifier or key conflicts to place in the pathology segment. Management comes next: TR21 and TR22 (Bethesda category to action), then TR8 (both keys, size bands), TR20 and TR27 (radioiodine, with TSH logic shown predict-then-show). Follow-up traps TR30, TR28 and TR16 form a ladder (calcitonin versus thyroglobulin, antibody qualifier, negative scan) and TR7 (staging age) sits with staging. Complications close the module: TR25, TR24, TR26. Order of meeting: TR1, TR5, TR4, TR11, TR12, TR10, TR3, TR6, TR21, TR22, TR8, TR20, TR27, TR30, TR28, TR16, TR7, TR25, TR24, TR26. Merged traps (TR2, TR9, TR13, TR17, TR19) ride on the probes of their host traps. Distractor_traps arrays run parallel to distractor_set; 'partial' marks a correct-adjacent option.
